title: Browse the destination list
intents: how many airports do we have
prose: I'll highlight Destinations in the sidebar.
This is the airport register — every station the airline and its caterers work through. The count beside the heading is the whole register; the list itself loads fifty at a time as you scroll.
Search narrows the list by code, city or country.
The list is the left half of a master-and-detail screen: choose a row here and its record fills the right.

And the screen never opens empty — it selects the first airport for you, so what you are reading on the right is that first record rather than anything you chose. Worth knowing before you act on it, and it is why Edit is available the moment the page loads.
notes: Route /setup/destinations, gated setup:destinations:read. Measured 2026-07-26: 161 destinations, 50 per page, scroll-triggered pagination. The first row is auto-selected on load. Two dead controls to be aware of: the funnel button beside the search has no onClick at all, and there is NO delete capability anywhere in this module — canDelete is commented out and the confirm handler only raises a 'not implemented' toast, so no delete recipe exists for it.

The list holds fifty airports at a time out of the full count shown beside the heading, and there is no More button — the next page is fetched when you scroll to within a few pixels of the bottom, so keep scrolling and the rest arrive. Scrolling is yours to do: I can highlight the list but I cannot scroll it for you in a way you would be able to follow. Four fields, and they are not equally reliable. The airport code is the one everything else in the system joins on — flights, contracts, stock and compliance all reach this airport through it, so it is the field to trust. Airport Type and Sector are descriptive and mostly unset in this register: a dash means nobody has recorded one, not that the airport is unclassified in reality. Airport Name is the full name for paperwork. To change any of them, use Edit at the top of the screen.

title: Check an airport's local time, timezone and cutoff
intents: what time is it at this airport
what is the timezone for MCT
what is the order cutoff at this airport

params.name: destination
params.description: Airport as a single searchable word — its code is the surest (MCT), a city name also works. NOT the full list label: the search box matches code, city or country individually, so "Muscat (MCT)" matches nothing.

prose: I'll highlight Destinations in the sidebar.
Opening the airport register.
Finding {destination}.
Opening its record.

This card carries the two figures that actually drive planning. Time Zone is stored as a plain offset from UTC, like +04:00 — it is text rather than a named zone, so nothing here follows a daylight-saving change on its own; if a country moves its clocks, somebody has to edit this field. Time Current is that offset applied to now, which is why it agrees with the field rather than proving it. Cutoff Time is the number of hours before departure after which orders for this airport close, and it is the field most likely to be wrong quietly: every airport in this register defaults to the same figure, so a station with a genuinely longer lead time will look normal until an order is refused. Address, City, Province and Country are the postal detail, dashes where nothing was entered.
notes: timezone is varchar and holds offsets such as '+04:00'; the displayed current time is computed from it, so the two can never disagree and the display is not evidence the offset is right. cutoff_hour defaults to 2 in the database and 4 in the create form's initial state — a created airport therefore starts at 4 while every seeded one reads 2.

Two separate switches, and the difference matters. Status is whether the airport is in use at all. Pressing View on Map.

This is a map search rather than a stored position: the airport's name, city and country are handed to the map provider as a query, so what you are looking at is that provider's best guess. For a well-known airport it lands on the terminal; for a sparse record — no name, or only a code — it can land on the city centre or somewhere else entirely. Treat it as a sanity check on the address rather than as coordinates we hold. Close it and nothing about the record has changed.

Opening the Add form. It arrives with sensible defaults already set: International, no sector, both statuses Active and a cutoff of four hours.
